The results leave the screen the moment you edit a field; press Calculate and they come back updated, so a single changed input shows its own effect.

sections.title: How does the Brake specific fuel consumption calculator work?
sections.html:
The Brake specific fuel consumption calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports power in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the units, the fuel type and the fuel type (2)); then you type in the fuel consumption, the fuel consumption (2), the BSFC (brake specific fuel consumption) and the BSFC (brake specific fuel consumption) (2).

Press Calculate once and the page holds the relationship, tracking which boxes you filled and working out everything else; from that point on it follows every edit you make.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Brake specific fuel consumption calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Power=3600 × fuel consumption ÷ BSFC (brake specific fuel consumption)
RPM=60000 × power ÷ torque
Power=(1 ÷ 33000) × RPM × torque
Efficiency=1 ÷ (BSFC (brake specific fuel consumption) × fuel type)

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

  • Flow rate mass, opening in grams per second
  • Flow rate mass, opening in pounds per second
  • Power, opening in kilowatts
  • Power, opening in mechanical horsepowers
  • BSFC - brake specific fuel consumption, opening in grams/kilowatt hour
  • BSFC - brake specific fuel consumption, opening in pound/horsepower hour
  • %, opening in percent
  • %, opening in percent

Display rounding is separate from calculation rounding: the digits you see are shortened, the value behind them is not. Numbers far from everyday size are shown in scientific notation so the significant digits stay readable.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Brake specific fuel consumption calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Testing how sensitive an answer is to one input
  • Turning a rough idea into a number you can act on
  • Checking a figure someone else quoted
  • Any time the same 3 figures keep coming back — the fuel consumption, the BSFC and the BSFC (brake specific fuel consumption) — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Brake specific fuel consumption calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns power, derived from the fuel consumption, the BSFC and the BSFC (brake specific fuel consumption). Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Brake specific fuel consumption calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the fuel consumption, the BSFC and the BSFC (brake specific fuel consumption), which is 8 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter fuel consumption in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Fuel consumption opens in grams per second and the chip beside it offers 16 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (3 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

faq.q: Is the Brake specific fuel consumption calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
